docs.title: Animal re-identification
docs.text:
This tool helps ecologists recognise individual animals in new photos by comparing them with photos of already known individuals, or with each other. It was developed for sea turtles. Instead of comparing whole images, each animal is split into body parts (head, front flippers, hind flippers), and each body part is compared separately.

The computer does the time-consuming work of searching through all photos and proposes the most likely matches. The final decision always stays with a human expert.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. Detection (automatic) – the TurtleDetector finds the body parts in every photo.
  2. Re-identification (automatic) – every body part in the new photos is compared with the same body part of the known individuals (identification), of the other new photos (discovery) or of the photos of the other individuals in the database (error detection).
  3. Verification (manual) – you check the most promising candidate pairs in the Image Comparator app.
  4. Assigning identities (automatic) – your answers are turned into one identity for every new animal (identification), into groups of photos of the same animal (discovery) or into a list of photos which are stored under a wrong identity (error detection).

docs.title: Terms used in this documentation
docs.text: Term Meaning Database Photos of individuals whose identity is already known. Query New photos whose identity you want to find. Encounter All photos of one animal taken at one occasion, for example on one day. Identities are assigned to whole encounters, not to single photos. Body part A part of the animal that is compared on its own: heads, front flippers or hind flippers.

docs.title: Identification, discovery and error detection
docs.text:
The workflow can be used in three ways.

Identification Discovery Error detection Used when There is a database of known individuals, for example a catalogue of photo-identified turtles. There is no such database, or the new photos contain many individuals that are not in it. There is a database of known individuals, which may contain mistakes. Question Which known individual is this? Which of these photos show the same individual? Which photos of different individuals show the same individual? Compared Query with database Query with itself Database with itself, only photos of different individuals Result Every query encounter gets an identity from the database, or is marked as new. Query encounters are grouped into individuals, and each group gets a new identity. Pairs of photos with different identities which show the same individual. Such identities are merged, or such photos are moved to the correct identity.

docs.title: Preparing photos
docs.text:
The photos are sorted into folders, and the folder structure tells the pipeline which photos belong to which individual or encounter. What is needed depends on the type of the project:

  • Identification needs two folders: the database with photos of known individuals and the query with new photos.
  • Discovery needs only the query with new photos.
  • Error detection needs only the database with photos of known individuals.

Species

The body parts are found by the TurtleDetector, which is trained on sea turtles. Other species need a different detector.

docs.title: Folder structure
docs.text:
Note

The structure below is only an example. Any other structure can be used, as described below.

IdentificationDiscoveryError detection 
my_project/
├── database/
│   ├── t001/
│   │   ├── IMG_0001.jpg
│   │   └── IMG_0002.jpg
│   └── t002/
│       └── IMG_0103.jpg
└── query/
    └── 2024-06-12/
        ├── encounter_01/
        │   ├── IMG_2001.jpg
        │   └── IMG_2002.jpg
        └── encounter_02/
            └── IMG_2010.jpg
  • Database: <identity>/<photo>. The folder name is the identity of the individual.
  • Query: <date>/<encounter>/<photo>. All photos in one encounter folder must show the same animal. The folder names can be anything, they only need to be different for different encounters on the same date.
my_project/
└── query/
    ├── 2024-06-12/
    │   ├── encounter_01/
    │   │   ├── IMG_2001.jpg
    │   │   └── IMG_2002.jpg
    │   └── encounter_02/
    │       └── IMG_2010.jpg
    └── 2024-06-13/
        └── encounter_01/
            └── IMG_2105.jpg
  • Query: <date>/<encounter>/<photo>. All photos in one encounter folder must show the same animal. The folder names can be anything, they only need to be different for different encounters on the same date.
my_project/
└── database/
    ├── t001/
    │   └── 2024-06-12/
    │       └── encounter_01/
    │           ├── IMG_2001.jpg
    │           └── IMG_2002.jpg
    └── t002/
        └── 2024-06-13/
            └── encounter_01/
                └── IMG_2105.jpg
  • Database: <identity>/<date>/<encounter>/<photo>. The first folder name is the identity of the individual, the other levels are the same as for the query.

In the notebook, the folder levels are set by levels in Dataset_FolderStructured:

IdentificationDiscoveryError detection 
dataset_query = Dataset_FolderStructured(root_query, levels=("date", "encounter"))
dataset_database = Dataset_FolderStructured(root_database, levels=("identity",))

dataset = Dataset_FolderStructured(root, levels=("date", "encounter"))

dataset = Dataset_FolderStructured(root, levels=("identity", "date", "encounter"))

If your folders have a different number of levels, change levels accordingly, while keeping these rules:

  • The database should always specify identity.
  • All photos must be exactly at the depth described above. Photos at another depth cause an error.
  • Supported formats are .jpg, .jpeg, .png, .tiff and .bmp.
  • Every photo should show only one animal. Photos with several animals of the same species can produce wrong matches.

Why encounters

Different photos of one encounter often show different body parts or different sides of the animal. Grouping them into an encounter combines the evidence of all photos into one prediction.

docs.title: Using custom dataset loaders
docs.text:
If the folder structure does not fit, or the identities and encounters are stored in a table, load the photos by any loader from wildlife-datasets and save its metadata as metadata.csv next to the photos. It must contain the columns image_id, path, identity and optionally encounter_id.

Warning

image_id must be text with at least 10 characters, and the query and database must not share any image_id. All computed results are stored under it. Create it from the paths by get_persistent_id(metadata["path"]) from wildlife_datasets.datasets.utils.

docs.title: Setting the folders in the notebook
docs.text:
In the notebook, set the paths to your folders and skip the cell that downloads the example data:

IdentificationDiscoveryError detection 
root_query = "path/to/my_project/query"
root_database = "path/to/my_project/database"
file_name_verification = "verification_data.csv"
file_name_answers = "answers.csv"
root_cache = "output/cache_my_project"

root = "path/to/my_project/query"
file_name_verification = "verification_data.csv"
file_name_answers = "answers.csv"
root_cache = "output/cache_my_project"

root = "path/to/my_project/database"
file_name_verification = "verification_data.csv"
file_name_answers = "answers.csv"
root_cache = "output/cache_my_project"

Use a different root_cache for every project.

docs.title: Local installation
docs.text:
The package can be tried without any installation in the notebooks for identification, discovery and error detection in Google Colab. The first code cell installs everything that is needed.

All commands are run in a terminal. If you have not used it before, the Image Comparator installation guide explains how to open it.

Step 1. Install Git and uv as described in Image Comparator.

Step 2. Download this repository and install it:

git clone https://github.com/sadda/turtle_re_id
cd turtle_re_id
uv venv
uv pip install -e ".[models]" jupyter

This creates a virtual environment in the .venv folder and installs the package into it.

Step 3. Activate the environment and start Jupyter:

Linux, MacWindows 
source .venv/bin/activate
jupyter notebook examples

.venv\Scripts\activate
jupyter notebook examples

Then open introduction.ipynb for identification, discovery.ipynb for discovery or error_detection.ipynb for error detection. The environment must be activated every time you open a new terminal.

docs.title: Installing Image Comparator
docs.text: The verification step uses the Image Comparator app. Install it by following its installation guide. It is installed separately and runs on your computer, not in Colab.

docs.title: Updating
docs.text:
To get the latest version, run in the turtle_re_id folder:

git pull
uv pip install -e ".[models]"

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
The fastest way to see the whole workflow is to open one of the notebooks in Google Colab:

  • Identification: new photos are compared with a database of known individuals.
  • Discovery: photos are compared with each other to find the same individuals.
  • Error detection: photos of a database are compared with each other to find mistakes in the identities.

The first run is slow, because all photos have to be processed. After that, adding new photos only processes the new ones.

Part When is it downloaded/computed Installing the packages once Downloading the models once Processing database photos once Processing query photos only for new photos

If you are satisfied with the functionality of the package and want to try more, the next step is to install the package locally and use it with your own data. This also avoids the limitation of Google Colab, which deletes all results when the session ends, so everything has to be computed again.

docs.title: Running the pipeline
docs.text: The notebook runs the detection, the re-identification and the export of the pairs for verification. This page describes what to change for your own data, what is stored between runs, and how to verify the pairs.

docs.title: Changes in the notebook
docs.text:
The notebooks are set up for the example data. For your own data, change only three things:

  1. Folders: set the paths to your photos and skip the cell that downloads the example data, see Preparing photos.
  2. Answers: the cell with true_identities only simulates the verification for the example data. Once answers.csv exists, the notebook loads it instead, see Updating the database.
  3. GPU (optional): if you have an NVIDIA GPU, set device = "cuda". The results are the same, only faster.

docs.title: What is stored
docs.text:
All computed results are stored, so the next run processes only new photos.

File or folder Content Notes segmentation.csv (next to the photos) Detected body parts The detection runs only for photos which are not in this file. Photos with no detection are stored too, so they are not processed again. root_cache Features and keypoint matches Use a different root_cache for every project. Changing img_load creates a new cache. verification_data.csv Pairs for verification Created again in every run.

Deleting anything in the output folder is safe, only the next run takes longer.

Warning

The results are stored under the photo's path. If you replace a photo by another one with the same name, the old results are kept. Delete segmentation.csv and root_cache in that case.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
The pairs for verification are checked in Image Comparator. After installing it:

IdentificationDiscoveryError detection
  1. Create a folder for the verification and copy verification_data.csv there.

  2. Create a config file my_project.json in that folder with the path to the folder which contains query and database:

    {
  "root": "/path/to/my_project"
}

  3. Open a terminal in that folder and run

    image-comparator identification --config my_project.json
  1. Create a folder for the verification and copy verification_data.csv there.

  2. Create a config file my_project.json in that folder with the path to the folder with the photos (root in the notebook):

    {
  "root": "/path/to/my_project/query"
}

  3. Open a terminal in that folder and run

    image-comparator discovery --config my_project.json
  1. Create a folder for the verification and copy verification_data.csv there.

  2. Create a config file my_project.json in that folder with the path to the folder with the photos (root in the notebook):

    {
  "root": "/path/to/my_project/database"
}

  3. Open a terminal in that folder and run

    image-comparator errors --config my_project.json

Answer every pair by Same, Different or Unknown. The answers are saved to answers.csv in the same folder. See the Image Comparator documentation for sharing the verification with other annotators.

Warning

Do not change the photos, metadata.csv or segmentation.csv between running the notebook and the verification. Image Comparator finds the photos of every pair through them.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Images must be exactly N folder(s) deep to match levels

Some photos are at a different folder depth than expected. Check the folder structure in Preparing photos. The error message lists some of the affected photos.

image_id must be strings with at least 10 characters

The image_id column in your metadata.csv contains numbers or short names. Create the ids from the paths with get_persistent_id, see Using custom dataset loaders.

Datasets 0 and 1 share image_id

A photo appears in both the query and the database, or two metadata.csv files use the same ids. Remove the photo from one of the folders.

All files are gone in Google Colab

Colab deletes all files when the session ends. For regular work, use the local installation.

The notebook is very slow

The first run processes all database photos and can take a long time on a CPU. The next runs process only new photos. If you have an NVIDIA GPU, set device = "cuda".

A turtle in the database was marked as new

None of its photos were among the proposed candidates. Check that the detected crops of this turtle look correct, see Updating the database.

Image Comparator says that answers.csv has wrong format

The answers.csv in the project folder belongs to an older verification_data.csv. Move it away and start the app again, see Updating the database.

Image Comparator says that files are missing

Run it from the folder that contains verification_data.csv and check root in the config file, see Verification.

docs.title: Contact
docs.text: In case of other problems, contact us by email.

docs.title: Updating the database
docs.text: The database grows with every round of verification: the identified animals are added to it, so that they help to identify future photos. Every round processes only the new photos.

docs.title: Loading the answers
docs.text:
After the verification, copy answers.csv from the Image Comparator folder next to the notebook, or set file_name_answers to its path. When this file exists, the notebook loads it instead of simulating the answers:

IdentificationDiscoveryError detection 
answers = pd.read_csv(file_name_answers)
predictions_verified = answers_to_predictions(answers)

answers = pd.read_csv(file_name_answers)
groups = answers_to_groups(answers)

answers = pd.read_csv(file_name_answers)
errors = answers_to_errors(answers, query_dataset.wildlife_dataset.metadata)

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
IdentificationDiscoveryError detection

Every query encounter gets one of four results:

Result Meaning What to do identity, e.g. t023 One candidate was answered Same. Move the photos to database/t023/. new All candidates were answered Different. Choose a new identity and move the photos to database/<new identity>/. conflict Two different individuals were answered Same. Check the pairs of this encounter again in Image Comparator. None No candidate was answered Same, but some were not answered. Answer the remaining pairs, or leave the encounter in the query for the next round.

Note

new means that the individual is not among the checked candidates. Rarely, an individual which is in the database was not proposed at all, and it is marked new too. If you know the population well, check the new encounters before giving them a new identity.

Remove the identified encounters from the query folder. Otherwise they are proposed for verification again.

groups contains one row for every group of encounters which were answered Same, directly or through other encounters. Every group is one individual: choose a new identity for it and move its photos to database/<new identity>/.

Note

Two encounters of one individual end up in different groups when no pair between them was proposed or answered Same, for example when the photos show opposite sides of the animal. Such groups are merged later, when the individual is photographed again.

Once the groups are in the database, continue with identification for the new photos.

errors contains one row for every pair of photos with different identities which was answered Same. The photos of each pair of identities show the type of the mistake:

Mistake How it looks What to do One individual stored under two identities Photos from several encounters of both identities are matched. Keep one identity and move the photos of the other one to its folder. Photo stored under a wrong identity Only one or a few photos of an identity are matched with another identity. Move these photos to the folder of the other identity.

Every answer is valid only for its pair of photos. A photo of one identity matched with a photo of another identity does not mean that all their photos show the same individual.

Note

Error detection is a check of the database, not a step of every round. Run it from time to time, for example before a larger round of identification, so that the mistakes do not spread to the new identities.

docs.title: Routine for new photos
docs.text:
1. Copy the new photos into the query folder.
  2. Run the notebook. The detection and the re-identification run only for the new photos and for the photos which were moved to the database.
  3. In the Image Comparator folder, move the old answers.csv away (for example to answers_2024-06-12.csv) and copy the new verification_data.csv there. Image Comparator refuses to start with an answers.csv which belongs to another verification_data.csv.
  4. Answer the pairs, load the answers and update the database as described above.

Tip

Keep the old answers.csv files. They document every identity decision.
